input: nums is an Array of n integers in [0,100000], with 0 <= n <=100000. Integer inputs, when present, are primitive safe-integer Numbers excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, proxies, subclasses or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The minimum number of unit increments needed to make all input values distinct, with each occurrence independently incrementable and no decrements permitted. Only the minimum count is returned; nums is not actually incremented. Empty input returns 0.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, caller containers and ordering remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state and separate calls share no mutable result state. Only a fresh sorted copy is reordered; assigned values are simulated by a scalar next_free. No modified array escapes.
numeric: The largest simulated assignment is at most 199999 and next_free at most 200000. The total increments are at most n*(n-1)/2 <=4999950000 because sorted item i needs at most i extra units. Counts may exceed signed 32-bit but remain exact safe integers. Sorting uses relational comparison.
complexity: O(n+1) greedy work after sorting. JavaScript sorting adds T_sort(n) time and O(n+S_sort(n)) auxiliary copied-array/workspace costs; ECMAScript does not prescribe a universal sort complexity. Each sorted value takes the earliest available integer at or above itself, minimizing its contribution without restricting later assignments unnecessarily.
